amazon.name: Amazon
amazon.process: Amazon typically conducts 4-5 rounds of interviews focusing heavily on Data Structures, Algorithms, and System Design, aligned with their 16 Leadership Principles.
rounds: Round 3: Onsite Loop (3-4 technical + behavioral rounds)

faqs.q: Do I need to know System Design for SDE-1?
faqs.a: Usually, SDE-1 roles focus on Object-Oriented Design (OOD) rather than full-scale distributed System Design.

faqs.q: How important are the Leadership Principles?
faqs.a: Extremely important. Amazon evaluates every candidate against them, especially the Bar Raiser.

tips: Use the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) for behavioral questions.
Practice medium and hard LeetCode problems, especially on Trees, Graphs, and DP.

google.name: Google
google.process: Google's interview process is highly technical, focusing deeply on CS fundamentals, complex algorithms, and analytical thinking.
rounds: Round 1: Online Assessment or Recruiter Screen
Round 2: Technical Phone Interview (Coding in Google Docs/CoderPad)
Round 3: Onsite Loop (4-5 rounds: 3-4 coding, 1 Googlyness/Leadership)

faqs.a: It evaluates how you work in a team, navigate ambiguity, and whether you do the right thing.

tips: Always think out loud. Google interviewers care more about your thought process than the final compiled code.
Be prepared to optimize your solution for time and space complexity.

microsoft.name: Microsoft
microsoft.process: Microsoft interviews test your problem-solving skills, coding fundamentals, and cultural fit. They often ask practical, scenario-based coding questions.

faqs.q: What kind of coding questions do they ask?
faqs.a: Standard DSA questions, often focusing on arrays, strings, linked lists, and basic system design for higher roles.

tips: Ensure you write clean, production-ready code on the whiteboard.
Understand Microsoft's core technologies and culture.

tcs.name: TCS
tcs.process: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) conducts the National Qualifier Test (NQT) for mass hiring, followed by technical and HR interviews. Roles include Ninja, Digital, and Prime.
rounds: Round 1: TCS NQT (Aptitude, Logical, Verbal, Programming Logic, Coding)

faqs.q: What is the difference between Ninja and Digital?
faqs.a: Ninja is the base profile. Digital is for candidates with advanced coding skills and offers a higher package.

tips: Strong fundamentals in C/C++/Java/Python are crucial.
Be prepared for questions on DBMS, SQL, and your final year project.

infosys.name: Infosys
infosys.process: Infosys recruits through InfyTQ and hackwithinfy platforms, offering roles like System Engineer (SE), Specialist Programmer (SP), and Digital Specialist Engineer (DSE).
rounds: Round 1: Online Test (Aptitude, Logical Reasoning, Verbal)

faqs.q: What topics are covered in the pseudo-code section?
faqs.a: C/C++/Java basics, output guessing, and basic logic.

tips: Focus heavily on logical reasoning and pseudo-code solving.
Be ready to explain every detail of the projects listed on your resume.
